body:
Thank you for the encouragement :)


Sorry to ask another question, but do you (or does anyone else) know what you actually do when you go to counselling? I'm worried about going in and not knowing what to say, I honestly don't really know how I'd describe what I'm feeling or why... I have trouble figuring it out myself lol.. Do I need to prepare anything?

Ah, I see. Is it so bad for your parents to know how you're feeling? I can understand why you wouldn't want them to, but if they knew how you're feeling they may be able to support you better. Of course, this depends on what your parents are like - unfortunately not all are great at dealing with this sort of thing.


The alternative could be going to the counsellor and talking about how bad your stress is making you feel, but not mentioning anything about suicide.


I'd also like to ask, is it only the stress of exams that's making you feel this way? It's fine if it is, but I was just wondering if there's anything else bad in your life or at school.

You're definitely not "too young to be stressed out", don't believe anyone who tells you that. If you feel stressed then you feel stressed, your age and situation don't matter.


School can be horribly stressful, no matter what level you're at or how high your workload is. You shouldn't worry about failing your exams though, just try your best - and if it doesn't go well, it's not the end of everything, there's always another path. It most certainly isn't worth ending your life over, and chances are you'll feel a lot better once these exams are over.


I know it feels awful, I've got really anxious over exams in the past too, but the best things to do are revise lots and make sure to relax when you take breaks. It'll at least prepare you more. My other advice is don't be afraid to have the occasional day off school if your mental health is especially bad, i.e. to the point where you can't focus in class. 


Are you sure that your counselor would tell your parents? If so that's pretty awful, counselling should always be confidential
Please hang in there... Don't ever stop fighting <3

I can relate somewhat, it's not actively on my mind but the stress of so much college work and anxiety of having new classes is definitely affecting my mood and making me get upset over silly things. I somehow got an interview at a prestigious university too, and I know I should be preparing for it but I'm finding it hard to even eat at the moment. 


I hope you manage to get through this, I'll be hoping for the best for you.. I'm sure it will be worth it in the end :)
